acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2002 and had two children. The respondent wife allegedly behaved cruelly, fought with the family, and made claims for separate accommodation. She left the matrimonial home several times but was brought back. The husband filed a divorce petition under Section 13(1)(ia) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1956.

legal_principles.principle: Mere acquittal in a criminal case cannot be a ground to hold that the respondent was not subjected to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The onus for proving the averments in the Criminal case are different from the Civil proceedings and mere acquittal cannot be a ground to hold that the respondent was not subjected to cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove the same.
legal_principles.held: It is asserted that the incident of alleged attempt to rape of the respondent also did not inspire confidence. It was thus concluded that the appellant was not able to prove any act of cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision to dismiss the divorce petition was upheld. The respondent wife's behavior did not constitute cruelty under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1956.
